problem: Standard VLN agents fuse continuous visual features (e.g., ResNet/ViT) with a pretrained text encoder in a jointly learned cross-modal module. This works poorly when only 10-100 expert trajectories exist. Realistic synthetic perception data is hard to generate, and vision-feature policies transferred from other simulators overfit to non-transferable visual idiosyncrasies.
motivation: Annotated embodied trajectories are expensive, so low-data VLN matters. If each panoramic view is converted into natural-language captions, the whole navigation problem lives in text space. Text-only LLMs can then (a) cheaply synthesize full perception+action trajectories, (b) act as a domain-invariant bridge between rendered (ALFRED/AI2-THOR) and real (Matterport3D) environments, and (c) make errors interpretable and editable.
key_idea: Replace continuous visual features with language: caption every navigable view with off-the-shelf BLIP (+ Deformable DETR objects), then fine-tune a text-only LLaMA to pick the next view by generating its caption, using GPT-4-generated synthetic text trajectories to fill the low-data gap.
insight: Working in text makes data synthesis trivial, and it is the synthetic data that drives the gain. With 10 real trajectories, LLaMA2-7B alone gets 11 SR on val unseen; adding 10k GPT-4 text trajectories gives 32 SR, close to NavGPT (34) at a fraction of the size. Generator quality matters: 2k trajectories from GPT-3.5 give 15.6 SR vs 31.1 from GPT-4. Scaling from 2k to 10k barely helps (31.1 to 31.6) because instructions seeded from one scene lack diversity, while 2k extra GPT-4-turbo trajectories seeded from 1000 diverse instructions push SR to 32.6. Language is also the more transferable representation: ALFRED pretraining hurts vision-based RecBert (100-shot unseen SR 19 to 15) but helps LangNav (17 to 24), and LangNav transfers zero-shot at 18 SR vs RecBert's 7. Language also adds value on top of vision: concatenating BERT caption features to RecBert's ResNet features raises full-data unseen SR from 47.1 to 48.8. Most errors trace back to bad captions: manual caption edits fixed 7 of 10 failed trajectories.
method: Vision-to-text perception: BLIP captions each navigable view (and Deformable DETR detects objects, with outdoor categories suppressed). Only captions were used in the synthetic-data study, since objects gave no significant gain there.

Prompt template: task description + R2R instruction + text history ('Step t: To your {direction} is {caption}; ... You chose: {caption}') + current observation ('To your 30 degree right is "{caption}". Details: {objects}').

Action as text: the LLM generates the caption of the chosen navigable view (or 'stop') via greedy decoding without constrained decoding. Training maximizes log-likelihood of the action tokens (behavior cloning).

Random-action data augmentation: with probability rho, take a random action and relabel the next action with the shortest-path expert, which exposes the model to off-path states. rho=0 for few-shot, rho=0.2 for full data.

GPT-4 synthetic trajectory pipeline: Phase 1 prompts GPT-4 with 3 real R2R instructions to write 10 new ones. Phase 2 prompts GPT-4 to write a 5-7 step text trajectory for each new instruction, conditioned on the CLIP-text-nearest real instruction/trajectory. This yields 10,000 trajectories for about $500.

Sim-to-real transfer: pretrain on 128K ALFRED instruction-following pairs, after merging four 0.25 m MoveAhead steps into one, adding ±30° heading jitter, augmenting to 12 views with random masking, and keeping only GotoLocation sub-trajectories. Then fine-tune on 0/10/100 R2R trajectories.
Vision+language fusion (case study 3): RecBert with each candidate view represented by ResNet-152 features concatenated with BERT-base caption features.

setting.backbone: LLaMA2-7B (fine-tuned) for main/synthetic-data experiments; LLaMA-7B (fine-tuned) for ALFRED transfer; BLIP captioner + Deformable DETR (frozen) as perception; GPT-4 (frozen) as synthetic-data generator only
setting.training_data: 10 R2R trajectories (1 scene) or 100 (2 scenes), mixed with 10,000 GPT-4-generated synthetic text trajectories. Optional: ALFRED pretraining (128K instruction-following pairs) or full R2R train (≈235K pairs with rho=0.2). The multi-task model adds 386K ALFRED pairs (621K total).
setting.observation: panoramic RGB converted to text (BLIP captions + detected object names) for each navigable view, with relative heading/elevation text
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (choose a navigable view by generating its caption, or stop)

results: With only 10 or 100 real R2R trajectories plus 10k GPT-4 synthetic text trajectories, LangNav (LLaMA2-7B) reaches 32/34 SR and 28/29 SPL on val unseen. The strongest vision-based few-shot baseline, DUET, gets 12/23 SR, and GPT-4 few-shot prompting gets 13 SR. LangNav approaches NavGPT (GPT-4, 34 SR / 29 SPL), which uses GT depth filtering. ALFRED→R2R transfer helps LangNav (100-shot unseen SR 17→24) but hurts RecBert (19→15). On full data LangNav gets 43.2 SR unseen (45.6 multi-task), well below vision SOTA such as ScaleVLN (78.1), though with a smaller seen-unseen drop.
limitations: On full R2R data it clearly underperforms vision-based SOTA (43.2 SR vs HAMT 65.7 / ScaleVLN 78.1 on val unseen). Language discards visual detail, and caption errors or ambiguity cause most failures.
Synthetic instructions seeded from one scene lack diversity (repetitive 'start at A, pass B, stop at C', single-floor, living areas), so scaling synthetic data saturates.
Only evaluated on discrete-graph R2R (plus ALFRED multi-task); unfiltered object detections add noise, so objects were dropped in the main synthetic-data experiments.
